question.leadin: The Saraiva-Cotegipe Law and the Rio Branco Law began this process in one country.
question.text: Name this process completed by the Golden Law in that country. The U.S. completed this process by passing the 13th Amendment. A description is acceptable.
question.answerHtml: abolishing slavery [or ending slavery; prompt on abolition with “what was abolished?”]
question.clue: The last major law of this type in the Western Hemisphere was promulgated by Isabel the Redemptress and was called the Golden Law for applying to some ten million Brazilians.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a defunct Cabinet position.
swap.text: This member of Franklin Pierce's cabinet later became the first and only president of the Confederate States of America.
swap.clue: Franklin Pierce's Secretary of War was this man, whose Vice President was Alexander H. Stephens.

question.text: The Liberator was published by Isaac Knapp and this man, who infamously burned a copy of the Constitution in 1854, calling it an "Agreement with Hell" for its support of slavery.
question.clue: Arthur and Lewis Tappan splintered from one society started by this man.

swap.text: This former president was that only presidential candidate.
swap.clue: He appointed Brigham Young as first territorial governor of Utah, which led to the first territorial capital being named after this president.

question.leadin: After enduring a disastrous first day at this battle, Ulysses Grant supposedly quipped "Lick 'em tomorrow, though."
question.text: Name this two-day Civil War battle, which began with a surprise attack from Corinth by Albert Sidney Johnston and P.G.T. Beauregard. This battle saw heavy fighting at a sunken road called the Hornet's Nest.
question.clue: Fought in 1862, the Confederate armies here attempted to drive the Union Army towards Owl Creek, but forces under Grant fell back towards an area that became known as the Hornet's Nest.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about Civil War Battles.
swap.text: Confederate forces led by Braxton Bragg defeated Union forces led by William Rosecrans in this 1863 battle fought in Georgia near Chattanooga, Tennessee.
swap.clue: By ordering his troops to stand and fight on Snodgrass Hill, George Thomas averted a complete disaster, which earned him the sobriquet "The Rock of" this battle.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the Cornerstone Speech.
question.text: It was given by this "Little Pale Star from Georgia" who addressed a "new government" founded on the principle that "the negro is not equal to the white man."
question.clue: This Whig joined with his in-state rival, Democrat Howell Cobb, to create the first incarnation of the Constitutional Union Party, which helped elect his close ally Robert Toombs to the Senate.

swap.leadin: Want to change American history? Just write a book!
swap.text: Abraham Lincoln reportedly asked this woman if she was "the little woman who wrote the book that started this great war" in reference to her novel Uncle Tom's Cabin.
swap.clue: This author stoked abolitionist sentiments with her novel featuring the wicked Simon Legree. When Lincoln met this author, he allegedly said "So you're the little lady who wrote the book that started this big war," a reference to her novel Uncle Tom's Cabin.

question.text: Proposed between the Leavenworth and Topeka constitutions, this pro-slavery constitution was so horrible that pro-slavery governor Robert Walker resigned to avoid enforcing it.
question.clue: It was defeated in two referenda largely due to that Seventh article, which is entitled after the controversial issue that it addresses, "Slavery."

swap.leadin: This battle saw Robert E. Lee defeat an army twice the size of his after crossing the Rappahannock.
swap.text: Name this May 1 to 6, 1863 battle, a major defeat for Joseph Hooker in northern Virginia.
swap.clue: The losing side of this battle ultimately blamed Oliver Howard for getting those XI corps ambushed and slaughtered, though the commanding officer invoked the third person in supposedly claiming it was "the only time he lost faith in" himself.

question.text: This Union general issued the special order offering land near the coast from South Carolina to Florida after he made his scorched-earth "March to the Sea."
question.clue: Nicknamed "Hump" by his men, his most famous exploit of the war was his destructive March to the Sea.

swap.text: A former President of the Continental Congress from this family was once thought to be the pseudonymous "Federal Farmer" arguing against ratification. A member of this family nicknamed "Light Horse" suppressed the Whiskey Rebellion.
swap.answerHtml: Lee [accept Richard Henry Lee; accept Henry Lee III or “Lighthorse Harry” Lee]
swap.clue: Another person with this surname was nicknamed "Granny" after losing the Battle of Cheat Mountain, but was later affectionately nicknamed "Marse."

question.leadin: One of the central figures in this event was advised to act as he did by Laurence Keitt.
question.text: Name this action depicted in a political cartoon subtitled "southern chivalry." This action was carried out by Preston Brooks.
question.answerHtml: caning of Charles Sumner [prompt on Brooks-Sumner affair by asking “what did Brooks do to Sumner?”]
question.clue: Henry Edmundson and Laurence Keitt blocked onlookers to this event from intervening, and its perpetrator was fined only $300 by the District of Columbia.

swap.text: Among the Mugwump leaders was this German-born reformer, a former Secretary of the Interior under President Hayes who spent time as editor for both the New York Evening Post and Harper's Weekly.
swap.clue: A long-legged caricature of this senator by Thomas Nast famously depicts him as a carpetbagger.

question.leadin: Nathan Bedford Forrest escaped from this fortification with his men in the middle of the night, angrily stating "I did not come here to surrender my command."
question.text: Name this Tennessee fort surrendered to the Union by Simon Bolivar Buckner in February 1862. The Union commander whose forces captured this location was celebrated by the press for his demand of an "Unconditional Surrender."
question.clue: On February 6, 1862, Grant's 15,000 Federals, supported by four navy gunboats, took Lloyd Tilghman's garrison. It opened the Tennessee River to US naval operations and forced Albert Johnston to retreat from Kentucky.

swap.text: An anti-slavery speech given at this East Coast university in February 1860 raised Lincoln's national profile. In 2014, it ended its namesake founder's policy of full scholarships for every student.

question.leadin: After he helped destroy some bridges following the Pratt Street Riot, he was arrested at his home in Cockeysville.
question.text: Name this member of a state militia, who famously petitioned for a writ of habeas corpus.
question.clue: Among those who cut the telegraph lines was this Confederate recruiter, who was subsequently detained without habeas corpus, leading to an ignored decision by the Taney court restricting Lincoln's powers.

swap.text: The practice of treating escaped slaves as contraband and not returning them to the Confederacy was established by Benjamin Butler by a declaration named for this place on Old Point Comfort in southeastern Virginia. This place was the launching point for George McClellan's Peninsular Campaign.

question.text: The Princeton disaster occurred after Robert Stockton replaced the gun designed by this naval engineer with his own. In addition to designing the Princeton, this man designed the USS Monitor.
question.clue: The Monitor was designed by this native of Sweden who also pioneered screw propellers and built the Destroyer in 1878.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about congressman Laurence Keitt, FTSNOP.
swap.text: Keitt used a pistol to hold off senators who attempted to rescue this man, a Massachusetts senator beaten by Preston Brooks.
swap.clue: He was later kicked off the committee after stopping plots to annex Santo Domingo.
